equation_request.abstract: Recently, it was shown that Repeat-Until-Success (RUS) circuits can achieve a $2.5$ times reduction in expected depth over ancilla-free techniques for single-qubit unitary decomposition. However, the previously best-known algorithm to synthesize RUS circuits requires exponential classical runtime. In this work we present an algorithm to synthesize an RUS circuit to approximate any given single-qubit unitary within precision $\varepsilon$ in probabilistically polynomial classical runtime. Our synthesis approach uses the Clifford+$T$ basis, plus one ancilla qubit and measurement. We provide numerical evidence that our RUS circuits have an expected $T$-count on average $2.5$ times lower than the theoretical lower bound of $3\log_{2}(1/\varepsilon)$ for ancilla-free single-qubit circuit decomposition.

specification.problem: Approximate a single-qubit unitary U (via Euler angles, here one Rz(theta)) to precision eps using a Clifford+T repeat-until-success circuit with one ancilla: a 2-qubit Clifford+T block W is applied, the ancilla is measured, outcome 0 means the data qubit received a block-encoded operator A approximating U, and outcome 1 triggers a correction and a retry.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Smallest instance: 2 qubits (q0 data, q1 ancilla). A fixed small Clifford+T block W that block-encodes a non-unitary single-qubit operator A=<0|_anc W |0>_anc on the data qubit. Check the success-branch operator, the success probability, and the expected T-count of the retry loop. Out of scope: the paper's probabilistic polynomial-time classical synthesis algorithm (randomized Diophantine/factoring search), full exact synthesis over Z[i,1/sqrt2], and the claimed 2.5x average numerical T-count reduction. The abstract does not give the actual RUS gate sequence, so any concrete circuit is a placeholder.

symbols.meaning: 2-qubit Clifford+T circuit on (data q0, ancilla q1)
success-branch operator on the data qubit, A=(<0|_{anc} \otimes I)W(|0>_{anc} \otimes I)
T-count of one attempt of W
expected total T-count of the RUS loop

equations.label: Block encoding on success
equations.description: Outcome 0 on the ancilla leaves the data qubit in A|psi>/||A psi||; outcome 1 leaves it in B|psi>/||B psi||.
equations.abstract_quote: Our synthesis approach uses the Clifford+$T$ basis, plus one ancilla qubit and measurement.
equations.justification: One ancilla plus measurement in a Clifford+T circuit implies a post-selected, generally non-unitary branch operator; the formula is the standard block-encoding form.
assumptions: Little-endian ordering: q0 is data, q1 is ancilla

equations.label: Success probability
equations.description: Probability of ancilla outcome 0. For a state-independent probability, A^\dagger A=p_s I, so A=sqrt(p_s)*V with V unitary.
assumptions: RUS usefulness requires A proportional to a unitary V near U

equations.label: Approximation criterion
equations.description: Success-branch operator in the sketch's form, with u,v in Z[i,1/sqrt2] and normalized to a unitary V=A/sqrt(p_s) within eps of U.
equations.justification: Taken from the sketch's matrix form. The abstract only says the RUS circuit approximates U within eps. The success-branch normalization is not derived in the abstract.
assumptions: Operator-norm distance modulo global phase is the accuracy metric
Exact form of u,v for the paper's construction is unknown

equations.label: Expected T-count of RUS loop
equations.latex: \mathbb{E}[T]=T_W/p_s \ \text{(upper bound; if the failure branch is restored by Cliffords)}
equations.description: With geometric number of attempts, mean attempts is 1/p_s, so the expected T cost is the per-attempt T-count over p_s.
equations.justification: Mean of a geometric distribution. The abstract compares expected T-count against the ancilla-free bound.
assumptions: Independent attempts, failure restored by Cliffords or a state-independent fixup
Failure branches may have different T costs; the formula is then modified

equations.label: Ancilla-free lower bound reference
equations.description: The reference bound the RUS expected T-count is compared against.
equations.abstract_quote: theoretical lower bound of $3\log_{2}(1/\varepsilon)$ for ancilla-free single-qubit circuit decomposition
equations.justification: Stated directly in the abstract. The claim is about the average ratio being 2.5, so E[T] is about 1.2 log2(1/eps) on average.
assumptions: Asymptotic/average statement, not a bound on every instance

registers.name: q0
registers.role: data qubit (Qiskit bit 0, rightmost in counts keys)

registers.name: q1
registers.role: ancilla, initialized to |0>, measured to flag success (0) or failure (1)

steps.description: Choose the target U (e.g. Rz(theta)) and eps. Classically find W over Clifford+T whose success branch A approximates U. The paper's randomized polynomial-time search is not reconstructed; use a fixed hand-chosen W in a toy instance.
Apply W from the gate set {h,s,t,tdg,cx} to q0,q1 starting from the ancilla in |0>.
Measure q1. If 0, the data qubit holds A|psi>/||A psi|| and the loop stops. If 1, apply the Clifford correction or restore a known state, then repeat.
Estimate the expected T-count as per-attempt T-count over success probability and compare with 3 log2(1/eps).

specification.measurement: Measure ancilla q1 only (classical bit 0 holds it). Outcome 0 means success. For a single-shot simulator, postselect on ancilla=0 and read the data qubit state or its statistics.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Retry on outcome 1. Compute the empirical success rate and the operator distance of the post-selected data state to U|psi>. Compute E[T]=T_W/p_s.
assumptions: Scope choice: a single Rz-like target on one data qubit with one ancilla
Mid-circuit measurement with classical control is available, or the loop is simulated by postselection
Success probability is bounded away from zero
The sketch's description of the fallback pattern, arccos(1/3) angles and the specific 1.2 log2(1/eps) cost is not established by the abstract
